subject.title: fix: preserve embedded prompt caching across room events and native Responses

question: Which trusted-turn classes should execute `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`: explicit owners only, owners plus trusted internal/system turns, or every turn not explicitly classified non-owner—and should denied classes still see those schemas?
rationale: The patch changes both authorization and capability disclosure for owner ambient events and missing sender identity; source, tests, and provider contracts cannot determine the intended permanent trust model.

options.title: Owners plus trusted internal turns
options.body: Deny non-owners and untrusted ambient events, preserve explicitly classified internal/system access, and keep schemas stable with the runtime gate.

options.title: Explicit owners only
options.body: Deny all missing-identity and ambient turns, retain stable visible schemas, and require every trusted caller to provide explicit owner classification.

options.title: Preserve current permissive unknowns
options.body: Continue denying only explicit non-owners and solve prompt-cache stability without changing unknown or internal execution semantics.

recommendation.title: Owners plus trusted internal turns
recommendation.body: Deny non-owners and untrusted ambient events, preserve explicitly classified internal/system access, and keep schemas stable with the runtime gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history spans the embedded runtime, provider routing, agent tools, and Codex lifecycle, providing the broadest ownership signal for this cross-surface trust decision.
